title: Common TypeScript Mistakes and Troubleshooting knowledge check

questions.prompt: What should a production-oriented TypeScript project demonstrate?
options: Type annotations as a replacement for authorization and validation.
A working happy path without tests or documentation.
Secrets committed into client bundles for convenience.
Explicit contracts, runtime validation, tests for failures, secure configuration and reproducible delivery steps.
questions.answer_key: Explicit contracts, runtime validation, tests for failures, secure configuration and reproducible delivery steps.
questions.explanation: Production readiness requires runtime, security, testing and operational evidence beyond type checking.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Common TypeScript Mistakes and Troubleshooting”?
options: A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with incorrect assertions and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with incorrect assertions and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Incorrect assertions”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Common TypeScript Mistakes and Troubleshooting”?
options: Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check confusing runtime and compile-time guarantees, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume runtime validation at trust boundaries is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Check confusing runtime and compile-time guarantees, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Confusing runtime and compile-time guarantees”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
